description: Sea-green, webbed with gold where it broke and broke again. It holds armour together, and gold has a way of turning up.
lore: Gold in the hand is always cold. The gold in this one is exactly as warm as the sea-green around it, and that detail still stops conversations. The mend is no setting, either: it runs the whole way through, filed and worked like trade goldwork, and it will not come out of the stone, nor the stone off it.

Handlers grade by the seams and argue the count — one school calls it a tally of seasons worked, the other says a stone is not a calendar. What the count means is not argued: this broke, and held, and broke again, and held. Armourers promise only that a plate carrying one comes apart later than it should, and often not at all. A stone that is mostly mend teaches a mend.

[[characters/2f7f1de9|Halvard]], the pedlar who walks his pack between the fires and [[lore/the_gold_agreement|prices in nothing but gold]], will buy one, sell one, carry one — and book it as stone, never as gold: gold that cannot be spent is not gold to him. Pressed once, he weighed a [[monsters/lava_salamander_2|Palemaw]] stone in his palm, said the difference between the two prices was the animal, and would not be drawn further. He does allow that carriers find more gold in a season than luck explains, and he counts his purse twice after trading with one.
